```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(conflicted)

source(here::here("R/utils.R"))
source(here::here("R/utils_viz.R"))


itpc_data <- read_csv("../data/Destrieux_final_itpc.csv") %>%
  dplyr::filter(type == "stim_itpc") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    subject = factor(subject),
    roi = factor(roi),
    task = factor(task),
    P = factor(P, levels = c("pre", "post")),
    T = factor(T, levels = c("real", "sham")),

    # Create combined condition factor
    condition = interaction(P, T, sep = "_")
  ) %>% select(-c("task", "type"))

# Display data structure
glimpse(itpc_data)

# Summary statistics
summary(itpc_data$value)
```
```{r}
# Difference-in-Differences 
# Y = (Post_Real - Baseline_Real) - (Post_Sham - Baseline_Sham)

```


```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# Your current data
# itpc_data has: subject, roi, task, P, T, type, value, condition

# Step 1: Reshape from long to wide format
itpc_wide <- itpc_data %>%
  # Create a combined condition label
  mutate(condition = paste(P, T, sep = "_")) %>%
  # Select only the columns we need
  select(subject, roi, condition, value) %>%
  # Pivot wider so each condition becomes a column
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = condition,
    values_from = value
  )

# Check the structure
glimpse(itpc_wide)
# Should have columns: subject, roi, pre_real, pre_sham, post_real, post_sham

# Step 2: Calculate difference-in-differences
rba_data <- itpc_wide %>%
  mutate(
    # Calculate change for Real tDCS
    real_change = post_real - pre_real,
    
    # Calculate change for Sham
    sham_change = post_sham - pre_sham,
    
    # Calculate difference-in-differences (your Y variable)
    Y = real_change - sham_change,
    
    # Optional: calculate average baseline for covariate
    baseline_avg = (pre_real + pre_sham) / 2
  ) %>%
  # Select columns for RBA
  select(Subj = subject, ROI = roi, Y, baseline_avg) %>%
  # Remove any rows with missing values
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Y))

# Step 3: Check your data
summary(rba_data)
head(rba_data, 20)

# Check for any issues
cat("Number of subjects:", length(unique(rba_data$Subj)), "\n")
cat("Number of ROIs:", length(unique(rba_data$ROI)), "\n")
cat("Total rows:", nrow(rba_data), "\n")


```
```{r}
# Create visualization to check the contrast
library(ggplot2)

# Calculate group-level statistics for each ROI
roi_summary <- rba_data %>%
  group_by(ROI) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_Y = mean(Y, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_Y = sd(Y, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = n()
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_Y))

# Plot distribution of Y values by ROI (top 10 ROIs)
top_rois <- roi_summary %>% slice_head(n = 10) %>% pull(ROI)

rba_data %>%
  dplyr::filter(ROI %in% top_rois) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = ROI, y = Y)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "Difference-in-Differences by ROI (Top 10)",
    subtitle = "Y = (Post_Real - Pre_Real) - (Post_Sham - Pre_Sham)",
    x = "Region of Interest",
    y = "Differential Change (Real - Sham)"
  )
```



```{r}
work_folder <- here::here("notebooks")
model_name <- "diff_y_baseline"
table_name <- glue::glue("{model_name}_data.txt")
data_file <-glue::glue("{work_folder}/{table_name}")  # Using a data file with a space

output_dir <- glue::glue("{work_folder}/results/{model_name}/{model_name}") # Using a path with a space
dir.create(output_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# Step 0: Export for RBA
write.table(
  rba_data,
  file = data_file ,
  sep = "\t",
  row.names = FALSE,
  quote = FALSE
)

# --- 1. Define variables (as you had before) ---

model <- 'Y~1+baseline_avg+(1|Subj)+(1|ROI)'
chains <- 4
iterations <- 4000
dist_y <- "student"

# --- 2. Construct paths safely ---
# Use file.path() instead of paste() with "/"
#prefix_path <- file.path(full_output_dir, model_name)

# --- 3. Define the command and its arguments ---
command <- "RBA"

# Each "word" the shell would see is its own element
args <- c(
  "-prefix",output_dir,
  "-chains", chains,
  "-iterations", iterations,
  "-mean", model,
  "-EOI", "Intercept",   # The single quotes aren't needed here
  "-ridgePlot", "10", "8", # "10" and "8" are two separate args
  "-distY", dist_y,
  "-dataTable",
  data_file
)

# --- 4. Run the command ---
# system2() is the modern and safe way to run commands.
# It handles all the quoting for you.

# If you just want to see the command string (e.g., for logging):
# You can paste the quoted arguments together
cat(command, paste(shQuote(args), collapse = " "))

#Wrap the call in tryCatch
result <- tryCatch({
  
  # --- 1. TRY ---
  # This code will run first.
  message("Attempting to run command...")
processx::run(command, args)
  
}, error = function(e) {
  
  # --- 2. CATCH ---
  # This code runs ONLY if processx::run() throws an error.
  message("Command failed!")
  
  # 'e' is the error object. For processx errors, 'e$stderr'
  # usually holds the error message from the external command.
  message("Error message from subprocess (stderr):")
  cat(e$stderr)
  
  # Return a value (like NULL or FALSE) to signal failure
  return(NULL)
})

# Output:
# RBA "-prefix" "results/my model/run_01" "-chains" "4" "-iterations" "2000" ...

  # Move ridge plot if it exists
  ridge_file <- "Intercept_ridge.png"
  if (file.exists(ridge_file)) {
    fs::file_move(
      ridge_file,
      glue::glue( glue::glue("{work_folder}/results/{model_name}/{model_name}_intercept_ridge.png"))
    )
  }
```

```{r}
library(here)
library(glue)
source(here::here("R/rba_helpers.R"))

# Step 1: Prepare and save data
work_folder <- here("notebooks")
model_name <- "diff_y_baseline"

data_file <- save_rba_data(
  data = rba_data,
  model_name = model_name,
  work_folder = work_folder
)

# Step 2: Run RBA
output_files <- run_rba(
  data_file = data_file,
  model_name = model_name,
  model = "1+baseline_avg",
  work_folder = work_folder,
  chains = 4,
  iterations = 4000,
  dist_y = "student",
  eoi = "Intercept,baseline_avg",
  qvars = "baseline_avg",
  stdz = "baseline_avg"
)

# Output files are automatically organized
#print(output_files)
```
